B2B Sales Strategy

Strategic Account Prioritisation Framework

A systematic framework for identifying, evaluating and prioritising high-potential B2B accounts, with an interactive illustrative matrix.

01Project title

Developing a Strategic Account Prioritisation Framework for Improving B2B Sales Effectiveness.

Conceptual framework This is conceptual project work, not a record of completed commercial outcomes.

02Business challenge

Sales teams have limited time. Without a consistent way to rank accounts, effort spreads evenly across accounts with very different potential.

03Objective

Develop a systematic framework for identifying, evaluating and prioritising high-potential B2B accounts.

04Evaluation dimensions

  • Account potential
  • Strategic fit
  • Revenue opportunity
  • Profitability
  • Relationship strength
  • Growth potential
  • Ease of service

05Interactive prioritisation matrix

Adjust how much each dimension matters and see how the ranking changes.

Illustrative only. The accounts and scores below are hypothetical examples to show how the framework works. They are not client data or project results.

Set the weights

Total weight: 100. Scores are normalised, so the total need not equal 100.

Resulting priority

#AccountWeighted scoreOut of 5Tier

Each account is scored 1–5 on every dimension; the weighted average sets the tier (Priority ≥ 3.8, Develop ≥ 3.0, otherwise Maintain).

B2G Market Research & Business Development

Government Department Opportunity Mapping

B2G opportunity mapping across 28 States and 8 Union Territories: 649 departments, 1,444+ officer-level contacts and 1,789+ department–product opportunities.

01Project background

Oizom Instruments makes environmental monitoring products. Government departments are a major buyer group, but the opportunity is spread across hundreds of departments in every State and Union Territory, each with its own mandates, budgets and decision-makers.

02Business objective

Build a structured, nationwide view of where Oizom's solutions fit within government, who the relevant officers are, and how to approach each department, so the sales team could run focused B2G outreach.

03Research methodology

Secondary research across government sources, translating national programmes into department-level needs:

  • National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)
  • Smart Cities Mission
  • CPCB Online Continuous Emission Monitoring (OCEMS) requirements

04Data collection approach

Information was gathered from government portals, budgets, policies, annual reports and Smart City initiatives, and organised into a structured government database.

05Department segmentation

Departments were organised State by State and UT by UT, giving each of the 36 regions its own profile, problem statement and proposal.

Departments profiled by State / UT

06Product mapping

For every department, the workbook records the major problems it faces, the recommended Oizom products, their key benefits and a tailored pitch. Matching needs to products produced 1,789+ department–product opportunities.

07Opportunity identification

Opportunities were qualified and prioritised with the PPVVC framework (Pain – Power – Vision – Value – Control), and 1,444+ officer-level contacts were identified across the 649 departments.

08Sales pitch development

36 State/UT-specific proposal presentations and 628 solution-oriented sales pitches were prepared, aligned to each department's needs, with reporting to the VP – Sales. A Customer Experience & Satisfaction Survey was also designed to support CSAT measurement.

09Key findings

  • Data platforms had the widest fit. Envizom, the environmental data platform, was recommended in 561 of 649 department profiles (86%), followed by Weathercom (428) and Polludrone (387).
  • Need spans well beyond environment departments. Profiles cover public works, rural development, mining, energy, urban development and public health engineering, not only pollution control.
  • National programmes anchor the pitch. NCAP, the Smart Cities Mission and CPCB OCEMS create monitoring needs at department level, which made them the starting point for each pitch.
  • Coverage was deepest in Arunachal Pradesh (29 departments), Uttar Pradesh (26) and Ladakh (25).

10Business implications

The database, qualification framework and pitch library give a sales team a prioritised starting point for government outreach across India, rather than starting from scratch in each State.

Marketing · Academic project

IMC Plan & Promotional Strategy: AXE

Redesigning a brand's promotional strategy to change its image and positioning: IMC objectives, budget, media plan and creatives across video, print, audio and digital.

01Overview

The final examination project for the MBA course on Integrated Marketing Communications: completely redesign the promotional strategy of a brand that needs to change its brand image and positioning to win consumer acceptance.

02The brief

Choose one category from men's innerwear, mouth fresheners, fairness creams, toothpaste, perfume / deodorant or cement, then narrow it down to a brand that urgently needs a new brand identity. The team chose AXE in the perfume / deodorant category.

03Deliverables

  • Brand and ad elements, where a redesign is needed
  • IMC objectives and budgeting
  • Media planning
  • Ad creatives: a video ad (TV, YouTube or social media), a print ad (newspaper, magazine or OOH), an audio ad (radio or Spotify) and two digital marketing formats other than video

04Assessment

A 10-minute presentation followed by a 10-minute viva, counting for 40% of the course grade (October 2026).

Sales Strategy & Opportunity Qualification

PPVVC Government Opportunity Qualification Framework

Pain – Power – Vision – Value – Control: a five-part lens for qualifying and prioritising government opportunities.

01Overview

PPVVC is a five-part qualification lens designed during the Oizom internship to judge which government opportunities deserve sales effort first.

P

Pain

Understand the department's existing challenges and requirements.

What problem must be solved?
P

Power

Identify decision-makers, influencers and stakeholders.

Who decides and who influences?
V

Vision

Understand the department's desired future outcomes.

What does success look like?
V

Value

Evaluate the commercial and operational value of the proposed solution.

Is it worth pursuing for both sides?
C

Control

Assess procurement readiness, decision processes, timelines and implementation considerations.

Can the deal actually move forward?

02Business challenge

With 1,789+ department–product opportunities identified, the team needed a consistent way to separate high-value, actionable leads from those unlikely to progress.

03How it prioritises opportunities

  • Pain and Vision show whether there is a real, mandated need and a clear target outcome.
  • Power confirms that the right officers and influencers are known.
  • Value tests whether the solution is worth it commercially and operationally.
  • Control checks procurement readiness and timelines, separating opportunities that can move now from those to nurture.

04The assessment worksheet

The framework is built as a workbook: 25 yes / unknown / no questions, five for each dimension. Every gap comes with a specific next step, so the assessment doubles as an action plan for the sales team.

Try the worksheet

Sample opportunity. The answers are pre-filled with the worked example from the assessment workbook. Change any answer to see the score and actions update. Y = 5, U (unknown) = 2.5, N = 0.

Pain

1. Is there an ongoing project requiring environmental monitoring?
2. Is there an upcoming project (0–24 months) where monitoring may be required?
3. Is the problem officially recognised in government plans, reports, DPRs, policies, or missions?
4. Is the problem significant enough to impact outcomes?
5. Is there urgency or a defined timeline?

Power

6. Minister/Department Head identified?
7. Secretary identified?
8. Operational decision makers identified?
9. Implementation agencies identified?
10. Verified stakeholder contact available?

Vision

11. Challenge mapped to Oizom product?
12. Supports department objectives?
13. Value proposition developed?
14. Benefits clearly explained?
15. Supports multiple products/platform?

Value

16. Funding likely available?
17. Improves compliance/efficiency?
18. Benefits measurable?
19. Commercially attractive?
20. Expansion potential?

Control

21. Procurement route understood?
22. Approval hierarchy understood?
23. Competitors identified?
24. Timeline understood?
25. Clear next step defined?
Overall score
3.9MEDIUM PRIORITY

Overall = average of the five dimensions. 4.0 or more is high priority, 3.0 or more is medium, below 3.0 is low.

Recommended actions

    05Where it was applied

    Used to qualify and prioritise public-sector targets within the government department opportunity mapping project, alongside an opportunity tracker (state, department, product, stage, value, probability and next action).
